title: Reading from the staff
summary: What the five lines mean, and where the tab went.

steps.title: Welcome
text: You already know where the notes are on the neck. This course teaches you to read them from standard notation instead of tab.
Each lesson explains one idea, shows it, then asks you to play it. Press **Next** to carry on.

steps.title: Five lines
text: Notation is written on a **staff** of five lines. The higher a note sits on the staff, the higher it sounds.
A note sits either **on a line** or **in a space** between two lines.

steps.title: The clef
text: The curly sign at the start is the **treble clef**. Guitar music has a small **8** under it, because the guitar sounds an octave lower than written.
You don't have to do anything about it. It is simply how guitar music is printed.

steps.title: The tab is still there
text: Whenever you are unsure, press **Peek tab** (or the **T** key) to see the tab under the staff. It is always free.
Here it is shown for you: four notes, with their names underneath.

steps.title: Try the controls
text: Press **Listen** to hear these four notes. Then find them on your guitar and play them slowly, using the tab.
When you have tried it, press **Next**.
